‘তোমার গাল বেশি নরম, হাতটা শক্ত’ — ছাত্রীকে হাবিপ্রবি শিক্ষক দীপক কুমার দিনাজপুরের হাজী মোহাম্মদ দানেশ বিজ্ঞান ও প্রযুক্তি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের (হাবিপ্রবি) ইংরেজি বিভাগের অধ্যাপক ড. দীপক কুমার সরকারের বিরুদ্ধে এক ছাত্রীকে অনৈতিক প্রস্তাব ও হেনস্তার অভিযোগ উঠেছে। ভুক্তভোগী ছাত্রীর লিখিত অভিযোগ অনুযায়ী, ২০২৫ সালের ২৩ জুলাই রাত ১টা ৫১ মিনিটে শিক্ষক তাকে হোয়াটসঅ্যাপে নক দেন। পরদিন বান্ধবীসহ দেখা করতে বলেন। অভিযোগে বলা হয়, কক্ষে একা পেয়ে শিক্ষক বলেন — “আমার জীবনে প্রথম যে প্রেমিকা ছিল, তুমি দেখতে ঠিক সেই মেয়েটার মতো। যখন তোমাকে দেখি, তখন আমার বুকের ভেতর আপস অ্যান্ড ডাউন হয়।” এরপর বিরলে চা খেতে যাওয়া ও ব্যক্তিগত সময় কাটানোর প্রস্তাব দেন। একপর্যায়ে হাত ধরে হ্যান্ডশেক করে বলেন — “তোমার গাল বেশি নরম, হাতটা শক্ত।” এ ঘটনায় মানসিকভাবে ভেঙে পড়েন ওই ছাত্রী। গত ১৭ নভেম্বর উপাচার্য, উপ-উপাচার্য ও রেজিস্ট্রার বরাবর লিখিত অভিযোগ দিয়েছেন তিনি। কিন্তু এখনও কোন পদক্ষেপ নেওয়া হয় নি, এজন্য যত বেশি পারেন এটা নিয়ে পোষ্ট করেন

🖥 Tehran summit: Environment a ‘silent victim’ of US-Israeli war on Iran 📌 Tehran, IRNA - War against people and war against nature are “expressions of the same state of mind,” American economist Jeffrey Sachs told a Tehran seminar, as Iran hosted an annual event marking the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict. Sachs, president of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network, addressed the seminar in a video message organized by the Center for Peace and Environment and the Water Diplomacy Association. ​ The event brought together scholars, civil society activists, media, and senior officials from Iran's environment, women, and peace ministries, along with representatives of UN and partner agencies based in Tehran. ​ In his remarks, Sachs argued that a leader who treats an adversary’s people as expendable is the same kind of leader “prepared to burn the fields, poison the wells, and foul the air.” ​ “A leader like Donald Trump, who decides that an adversary’s people do not count and that overwhelming force can settle a political problem, is the same kind of leader who is prepared to burn the fields, poison the wells, and foul the air,” he said. ​ He also cited historical cases from ancient Shechem to the US use of Agent Orange in Vietnam and Iraq's chemical weapons attacks, including at Sardasht in 1987, as other examples of this mindset. ​ “A political system that treats nature as something to be plundered for short-term profit finds it all too easy to treat other peoples in the same way,” Sachs added. ​ He pointed to the war in Gaza, citing a September 2025 UN Environment Programme assessment that found unprecedented damage to Gaza’s soils, freshwater supplies, and coastline, with recovery from some damage potentially taking decades. ​ The professor said Gaza had lost about 97 percent of its tree crops and 95 percent of its shrubland, and that by late July 2025, 86 percent of agricultural land had been damaged. ​ “The destruction of Gaza’s land, water, and trees cannot be separated from the brutal and brazen destruction of its people. They are one campaign.” ​ Turning to Iran, Sachs described the June 2025 12-day war and a larger US-Israeli war that began on February 28, 2026, which he condemned as “a brazen and illegal war launched without justification from the United Nations Security Council.” ​ “This is a brazen and illegal war launched without justification from the United Nations Security Council, of course, with no armed attack preceding by Iran that could conceivably justify ‘self-defense’ under Article 51 and in stark violation of the UN’s Charter prohibition on the use of force.” ​ He said airstrikes on March 7, 2026 hit four oil storage and refinery sites in and around Tehran, blanketing a metropolitan area of more than 9 million people in smoke and “oil-laden black rain” contaminated with sulphuric compounds and trace metals. ​ “The toxic chemicals, persistent pollutants,

🤥 Trump weighs new strikes on Iran as peace talks stall The risk of a renewed US bombing campaign on Iran has risen in recent days, Bloomberg reported, citing Western officials. One source said President Donald Trump was considering a new round of strikes and had yet to make a decision. 👉 The US struck Iran’s Qeshm Island on Tuesday and continues to enforce a naval blockade of Iranian ports. European and Gulf Arab governments are urging the US to avoid another major campaign, fearing Iranian retaliation across the region. Qatari officials met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Oman this week, with no sign of a breakthrough. Tehran says the US must lift the blockade before peace talks can resume, while the US is seeking concessions on Iran’s nuclear program. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
